# reifydb_build - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/reifydb-build/^0.7.0/

## Expand description

Build-time helper called from each downstream crate’s `build.rs` to resolve the `reifydb_target` and
`reifydb_single_threaded` cfg flags that gate platform-specific code paths. Nothing else in the workspace runs
this code; it exists purely to keep target-detection logic in one place.

---

# reifydb_rql - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/reifydb-rql/0.7.0/target-redirect/reifydb_rql/

## Expand description

ReifyDB Query Language: lexer, parser, AST, logical and physical planning, optimisation, and the instruction stream consumed by the engine VM. This is the full pipeline that turns a source string into something executable.

The crate exposes the AST shape so external tooling (formatters, linters, the explain renderer) can inspect queries without re-parsing, and exposes a stable fingerprint over compiled plans that the engine uses for plan caching. Diagnostics produced here carry source-fragment context so user-visible failures can point at the offending span.

Invariant: planner output is decoupled from any specific storage backend. The physical plan is expressed in terms
of `core::interface/` traits; concrete backend selection happens later, in the engine. Reaching into a specific
backend from inside the planner couples this crate to the storage tier and breaks the layering that lets `core`
avoid cycles.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [ast](https://docs.rs/ast/index.html)
- Abstract syntax tree for RQL. The parser entry point `parse_str`tokenises a source string and emits an`AstStatement`tree allocated in a bump arena tied to the source lifetime, so spans inside the AST can refer back to fragments of the original text without copying.
- [bump](https://docs.rs/bump/index.html)
- [compiler](https://docs.rs/compiler/index.html)
- [diagnostic](https://docs.rs/diagnostic/index.html)
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- [expression](https://docs.rs/expression/index.html)
- Planner-side expression representation. Mirrors the AST’s expression shapes but in a form that has been type-checked, name-resolved, and stripped of source-only details. The engine consumes these expressions to evaluate filters, projections, and join conditions; routine call resolution and JSON-path navigation are part of this representation rather than the runtime.
- [fingerprint](https://docs.rs/fingerprint/index.html)
- [flow](https://docs.rs/flow/index.html)
- RQL planning for CREATE FLOW. Analyses the source query, builds the operator graph, plans each operator
against the catalog, and produces the persisted flow definition the engine hands to `sub-flow`at runtime. Dataflow shape - which operator depends on which - is settled here, not in the streaming runtime.
- [instruction](https://docs.rs/instruction/index.html)
- [nodes](https://docs.rs/nodes/index.html)
- [optimize](https://docs.rs/optimize/index.html)
- Physical-plan post-passes. Walks the lowered plan and applies expression-level rewrites - constant folding,
projection simplification - that were not worth doing during logical compilation. New optimisations register
through the same `walk_expressions_mut`interface so they can be composed without re-traversing the plan once per pass.
- [plan](https://docs.rs/plan/index.html)
- Two-stage planner. `compile_logical`resolves names, type-checks, and produces a logical plan in terms of`core::interface/`primitives;`compile_physical`lowers that into the executable shape the engine VM consumes.`plan_with_policy`is the variant that interleaves a policy-injection pass between the two stages so read filters land before the physical lowering.
- [query](https://docs.rs/query/index.html)
- [token](https://docs.rs/token/index.html)

---

[52](#52)pub(crate) fn convert_data_type(ast: &BumpFragment<'_>) -> Result<ValueType> {
[53](#53)	Ok(match ast.text().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
[54](#54)		"bool" => ValueType::Boolean,
[55](#55)		"boolean" => ValueType::Boolean,
[56](#56)		"float4" => ValueType::Float4,
[57](#57)		"float8" => ValueType::Float8,
[58](#58)		"int1" => ValueType::Int1,
[59](#59)		"int2" => ValueType::Int2,
[60](#60)		"int4" => ValueType::Int4,
[61](#61)		"int8" => ValueType::Int8,
[62](#62)		"int16" => ValueType::Int16,
[63](#63)		"uint1" => ValueType::Uint1,
[64](#64)		"uint2" => ValueType::Uint2,
[65](#65)		"uint4" => ValueType::Uint4,
[66](#66)		"uint8" => ValueType::Uint8,
[67](#67)		"uint16" => ValueType::Uint16,
[68](#68)		"utf8" => ValueType::Utf8,
[69](#69)		"text" => ValueType::Utf8,
[70](#70)		"date" => ValueType::Date,
[71](#71)		"datetime" => ValueType::DateTime,
[72](#72)		"time" => ValueType::Time,
[73](#73)		"duration" => ValueType::Duration,
[74](#74)		"uuid4" => ValueType::Uuid4,
[75](#75)		"uuid7" => ValueType::Uuid7,
[76](#76)		"identityid" | "identity_id" => ValueType::IdentityId,
[77](#77)		"blob" => ValueType::Blob,
[78](#78)		"int" => ValueType::Int,
[79](#79)		"uint" => ValueType::Uint,
[80](#80)		"decimal" => ValueType::Decimal,
[81](#81)		_ => {
[82](#82)			return Err(AstError::UnrecognizedType {
[83](#83)				fragment: ast.to_owned(),
[84](#84)			}
[85](#85)			.into());
[86](#86)		}
[87](#87)	})
[88](#88)}
[89](#89)
[90](#90)pub(crate) fn convert_data_type_with_constraints(ast: &AstType) -> Result<TypeConstraint> {
[91](#91)	match ast {
[92](#92)		AstType::Unconstrained(name) => {
[93](#93)			let base_type = convert_data_type(name)?;
[94](#94)			Ok(TypeConstraint::unconstrained(base_type))
[95](#95)		}
[96](#96)		AstType::Constrained {
[97](#97)			name,
[98](#98)			params,
[99](#99)		} => {
[100](#100)			let base_type = convert_data_type(name)?;
[101](#101)
[102](#102)			let constraint = match (base_type.clone(), params.as_slice()) {
[103](#103)				(ValueType::Utf8, [AstLiteral::Number(n)]) => {
[104](#104)					let max_bytes = parse_number_literal(n.value())? as u32;
[105](#105)					Some(Constraint::MaxBytes(max_bytes.into()))
[106](#106)				}
[107](#107)				(ValueType::Blob, [AstLiteral::Number(n)]) => {
[108](#108)					let max_bytes = parse_number_literal(n.value())? as u32;
[109](#109)					Some(Constraint::MaxBytes(max_bytes.into()))
[110](#110)				}
[111](#111)				(ValueType::Int, [AstLiteral::Number(n)]) => {
[112](#112)					let max_bytes = parse_number_literal(n.value())? as u32;
[113](#113)					Some(Constraint::MaxBytes(max_bytes.into()))
[114](#114)				}
[115](#115)				(ValueType::Uint, [AstLiteral::Number(n)]) => {
[116](#116)					let max_bytes = parse_number_literal(n.value())? as u32;
[117](#117)					Some(Constraint::MaxBytes(max_bytes.into()))
[118](#118)				}
[119](#119)				(ValueType::Decimal, [AstLiteral::Number(p), AstLiteral::Number(s)]) => {
[120](#120)					let precision = parse_number_literal(p.value())? as u8;
[121](#121)					let scale = parse_number_literal(s.value())? as u8;
[122](#122)					Some(Constraint::PrecisionScale(precision.into(), scale.into()))
[123](#123)				}
[124](#124)
[125](#125)				_ => None,
[126](#126)			};
[127](#127)
[128](#128)			match constraint {
[129](#129)				Some(c) => Ok(TypeConstraint::with_constraint(base_type, c)),
[130](#130)				None => Ok(TypeConstraint::unconstrained(base_type)),
[131](#131)			}
[132](#132)		}
[133](#133)		AstType::Optional(inner) => {
[134](#134)			let inner_tc = convert_data_type_with_constraints(inner)?;
[135](#135)			Ok(TypeConstraint::unconstrained(ValueType::Option(Box::new(inner_tc.get_type()))))
[136](#136)		}
[137](#137)		AstType::Qualified {
[138](#138)			name,
[139](#139)			..
[140](#140)		} => Err(AstError::UnrecognizedType {
[141](#141)			fragment: name.to_owned(),
[142](#142)		}
[143](#143)		.into()),
[144](#144)	}
[145](#145)}
[146](#146)
[147](#147)fn parse_number_literal(s: &str) -> Result<usize> {
[148](#148)	s.parse::<usize>().map_err(|_| internal_error!("Invalid number literal: {}", s))
[149](#149)}
[150](#150)
[151](#151)use reifydb_core::interface::version::{ComponentType, HasVersion, SystemVersion};
[152](#152)
[153](#153)pub struct RqlVersion;
[154](#154)
[155](#155)impl HasVersion for RqlVersion {
[156](#156)	fn version(&self) -> SystemVersion {
[157](#157)		SystemVersion {
[158](#158)			name: env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME")
[159](#159)				.strip_prefix("reifydb-")
[160](#160)				.unwrap_or(env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME"))
[161](#161)				.to_string(),
[162](#162)			version: env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION").to_string(),
[163](#163)			description: "ReifyDB Query Language parser and planner module".to_string(),
[164](#164)			r#type: ComponentType::Module,
[165](#165)		}

# reifydb_rql::ast - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/reifydb-rql/0.7.0/reifydb_rql/ast/index.html

## Expand description

Abstract syntax tree for RQL. The parser entry point `parse_str` tokenises a source string and emits an
`AstStatement` tree allocated in a bump arena tied to the source lifetime, so spans inside the AST can refer
back to fragments of the original text without copying.

AST shapes are public so external tooling - formatters, linters, the explain renderer - can inspect parsed queries without re-parsing them. Adding or renaming a public AST node is a breaking change for that tooling.

---

# reifydb_rql::expression - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/reifydb-rql/0.7.0/reifydb_rql/expression/index.html

## Expand description

Planner-side expression representation. Mirrors the AST’s expression shapes but in a form that has been type-checked, name-resolved, and stripped of source-only details. The engine consumes these expressions to evaluate filters, projections, and join conditions; routine call resolution and JSON-path navigation are part of this representation rather than the runtime.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

# reifydb_rql::flow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/reifydb-rql/0.7.0/reifydb_rql/flow/index.html

## Expand description

RQL planning for CREATE FLOW. Analyses the source query, builds the operator graph, plans each operator
against the catalog, and produces the persisted flow definition the engine hands to `sub-flow` at runtime.
Dataflow shape - which operator depends on which - is settled here, not in the streaming runtime.

---

# reifydb_rql::optimize - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/reifydb-rql/0.7.0/reifydb_rql/optimize/index.html

## Expand description

Physical-plan post-passes. Walks the lowered plan and applies expression-level rewrites - constant folding,
projection simplification - that were not worth doing during logical compilation. New optimisations register
through the same `walk_expressions_mut` interface so they can be composed without re-traversing the plan once
per pass.

---

# reifydb_rql::plan - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/reifydb-rql/0.7.0/reifydb_rql/plan/index.html

## Expand description

Two-stage planner. `compile_logical` resolves names, type-checks, and produces a logical plan in terms of
`core::interface/` primitives; `compile_physical` lowers that into the executable shape the engine VM consumes.
`plan_with_policy` is the variant that interleaves a policy-injection pass between the two stages so read
filters land before the physical lowering.

The split lets policy and optimisation operate on a backend-neutral representation; nothing in the logical layer knows whether the table it reads from is a single-version or multi-version store.

---
